getLawyer.why: If arrested in Jamaica, ask to contact the Canadian High Commission (1-876-926-1500) and get a local lawyer; say nothing and sign nothing without counsel. Canadian officials can't interfere in Jamaica's judicial affairs. Dual Canadian/Jamaican citizens may get only limited consular help.

Penalties for drug possession, use, or trafficking are severe (lengthy prison). Departing visitors are thoroughly screened and cruise passengers may be searched — ask for a witness. NEVER carry anyone else's packages, and do NOT carry any cannabis into or out of Jamaica. Contact the High Commission and a lawyer.
Entering Jamaica with a firearm — or even a SINGLE round of ammunition — is a serious crime. Check every bag before you fly. If charged, contact the High Commission and a lawyer immediately.

deadlines.title: Visa-free stay — 90 days (extendable 90)
deadlines.rule: No visa for tourist/business/student/work stays up to 90 DAYS; officers usually grant 90 days' visitor status, extendable by up to 90 more at an immigration office. Overstaying is a CRIMINAL offence (prison, heavy fines, deportation). Keep your landing card to show on departure.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Jamaica

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (Jamaica)
sentencing.first_offender: Possession/use or trafficking of controlled drugs can bring lengthy prison sentences; carrying cannabis across the border is an offence regardless of local decriminalization.

sentencing.name: Firearm / ammunition (Jamaica)
sentencing.mandatory_minimum: Treated as a serious crime even for a single round.
sentencing.first_offender: Bringing in a firearm or any ammunition is a serious offence with substantial prison exposure.

statutes.title: Cannabis (ganja) — decriminalized to 2 oz, but limits
statutes.summary: Possession of up to 2 ounces of cannabis is decriminalized (a fine, no criminal record). Smoking in public remains prohibited. Do NOT carry any amount into or out of Jamaica — cross-border carrying is still an offence.

statutes.title: Camouflage clothing + conduct offences
statutes.summary: Wearing, buying, or selling army/police camouflage clothing is illegal. Nude sunbathing outside designated areas and using indecent language are also offences.

statutes.title: Police checkpoints — carry ID, cooperate
statutes.summary: Police checkpoints are common (especially the A1 North Coast Highway). Carry valid ID and cooperate. If searched when departing (cruise from Ocho Rios/Montego Bay), you may ask for a witness.

resources.name: Canadian High Commission (Kingston)
resources.note: Also 1-844-880-6519. 3 West Kings House Rd, Kingston 10.

book.title: Police, checkpoints, and your rights in Jamaica
book.overview: Jamaica is a common-law country. Police checkpoints are common — carry ID and cooperate. If arrested, contact the Canadian High Commission (1-876-926-1500) and a local lawyer; say and sign nothing without counsel. Emergencies: 119 police, 911 ambulance/fire.
your_rights: Carry valid ID; cooperate at checkpoints.
If arrested, contact the High Commission and get a lawyer.
If searched on departure, you may ask for a witness.
Do not sign anything without a lawyer.
Dual Canadian/Jamaican citizens may get limited consular help.
key_steps: Carry ID; expect checkpoints (esp. the A1).
If detained: ask for the High Commission and a lawyer.
Pack your own bags; never carry others' packages.
Save 119 / 911 and the High Commission line.
Keep your landing card for departure.
common_mistakes: Carrying any ammunition or a firearm.
Assuming dual citizenship gives full consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on any arrest, drug, or firearm matter — contact the High Commission and a local lawyer.

book.title: Entry and your stay in Jamaica
book.overview: No visa for stays up to 90 days (extendable 90 more). Overstaying is a criminal offence (prison, fines, deportation). Working illegally can mean detention until your return is arranged, at your own cost.
your_rights: Visa-free up to 90 days; extend up to 90 more at immigration.
You're entitled to your landing record.
You can request an extension before your status expires.
key_steps: Complete immigration info online or a paper landing card.
Keep the landing card for departure.
Track your 90 days; extend before they run out.
Carry proof of onward travel and funds if asked.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays or detention, consult a Jamaican lawyer via the High Commission.

book.title: Laws that catch tourists off guard in Jamaica
book.overview: Drugs, firearms/ammunition, cannabis across the border, and camouflage clothing are the big traps. Cannabis up to 2 oz is decriminalized (fine only) but public smoking and any cross-border carrying remain illegal. Same-sex sexual acts are criminalized (rarely enforced, up to 10 years) — avoid risk and know the law.
your_rights: Presumption of innocence; right to a lawyer.
Right to contact the High Commission.
If searched on departure, you may ask for a witness.
key_steps: Never carry cannabis into or out of Jamaica.
Check every bag for stray ammunition before flying.
If accused, say nothing and get a lawyer + High Commission.
common_mistakes: A single forgotten round in a bag.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately — a local criminal lawyer and the High Commission for any charge.

book.title: Emergencies, driving, and staying safe in Jamaica
book.overview: Emergencies: 119 police, 911 ambulance/fire. Traffic drives on the LEFT; a Canadian licence is valid up to 6 months. Helmets and seatbelts are mandatory (heavy fines). Use only JUTA-authorized taxis (red/white 'PP' plates, lime-green sticker) and agree the fare first. Between Norman Manley airport and Kingston, use South Camp Road.
your_rights: The High Commission has a 24/7 line via Ottawa.
You can report crime and get a reference for insurance.
key_steps: Drive on the left; carry ID for checkpoints.
Use JUTA taxis; agree fare first.
In danger, call 119 first, then the High Commission.
common_mistakes: Taking the Mountain View Ave route from the airport.
Not reporting a crime for insurance.
book.when_lawyer: For injury or a serious crime against you, the High Commission can refer local lawyers.
